root_idea.summary: The root centers on continuous accompaniment: one thing remains with, adheres to, or is inseparable from another.
root_idea.development: This orientation develops into remaining attached, imposing or becoming bound by an obligation, making something adhere as an assigned consequence, and requiring or entailing something necessarily.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form IV has distinct causative uses of compelling and making something adhere or become binding.
Quran-attested nominal form with the binding or inevitable sense.

senses.definition: 1. To compel or oblige someone to accept or comply with something.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative construction in which a person is brought under an obligation through command, judgment, or imposed necessity; the Quranic usage includes compelling acceptance of a matter.

senses.definition: 2. To make a thing, condition, or consequence adhere to someone, or to make people adhere to something; to assign it as inseparably binding.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for causatively fastening or imposing something so that it remains attached or necessarily accompanies the person or group; this includes the attachment of a person's assigned condition or works and the imposition of adherence to a principle.

senses.definition: 1. Something binding or inevitable; an outcome or condition that necessarily remains incumbent or comes to pass.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrences, the noun presents binding necessity; context may render it as an obligation or as something inevitable. The contextual association with punishment does not create a separate lexical sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To belong or pertain inseparably to someone or something; to remain attached, keep close, stay with, or retain it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes staying at a place without leaving it, adhering to a debtor, and preserving or keeping a thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be incumbent or obligatory upon someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the management of an affair, the payment of money, or another responsibility that lies upon a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To keep close to, confine oneself to, cling to, or continue with someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III expresses sustained or continual adherence to the object or activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impose an obligation on someone—to make him accept proof, perform an act, pay money, or undergo or endure something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are broader Classical applications of the Form IV causative beyond the specific Quranic contexts represented above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take an affair upon oneself, assume responsibility for it, or bind oneself to its obligation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes making oneself answerable or accountable for property, payment, or work.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To restrict oneself to an action or usage, and thereby become bound or obligated to perform, pay, suffer, or endure it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction concerns self-imposed adherence or obligation.
Attested in the cited idiomatic construction involving taking someone by the hand and embracing him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To necessarily require, entail, or involve something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is presented as a necessary implication or concomitant of another matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who keeps, cleaves, clings, or holds fast habitually to a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive or habitual description of persistent adherence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Imposing upon oneself what is not indispensable; in rhetoric, adhering to a mode of construction that need not be followed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional technical expression concerning unnecessary self-imposition or formal adherence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Adherent, tenacious, or inseparable; a necessary accompaniment, consequence, or result.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective describes what remains closely attached; the plural لوازم denotes necessary adjuncts or consequences.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most preservative; most conducive to preserving or safeguarding something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested as a synonym of أَقْنَى in a proverb concerning what best preserves modesty.

cautions: The Form IV Quranic usages distinguish compelling or obliging someone from making an item or consequence adhere to someone; translations may alternate between these patterns.
For لِزَام, “obligation” and “inevitable” represent the same binding-necessity notion in context; “punishment” is contextual rather than a separate lexical sense.
A Lane Quran citation associated with the attachment/decree discussion is not used here as an additional modern verse location; the examples use only secure QAC locations.
